chunks: From him, from Al-Haytham ibn Waqid, from Al-Hasan ibn Abdillah Al-Arrajani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever prays in his home, then goes to one of their mosques and prays in it, his good deeds will be counted for them.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying at home and then going to the mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the superior merit of congregational prayer (*Salat al-Jama'ah*) by indicating that the individual who prays at home and then joins the congregation receives the combined reward of both prayers. Scholars interpret this as a significant incentive for Muslims to prioritize mosque attendance, emphasizing that the communal act amplifies the spiritual value of the individual devotion. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the mosque is not merely a physical space but a locus of collective spiritual elevation.
